title: Cellular internalization, cytotoxicity and DNA binding property of 2,3-diaminophenazine, synthesized using Jeanbandyite, a heterogeneous catalyst.
authors: Sen, Subhadeep; Basak, Subhankar; Pandit, Samit; Sarkar, Pappu; Kim, Tae Wan; Ghosh, Nandan; Kong, Hye Jeong; Ryu, Jae Sung; Singh, Bhagat; Roy, Rosni; Mondal, Rajib; Saha, Abhijit; Jeon, Seob; Bhattacharya, Sumantra; Im, Jungkyun; Biswas, Goutam
one_liner_zh: 该文主要研究2,3-二氨基吩嗪的合成、细胞摄取、细胞毒性及与DNA的结合，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-DNA互作，非蛋白质-DNA体系，且方法以实验为主，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: In recent years, the development of novel chemistry routes for the synthesis of organic compounds has attracted special attention. 2,3-Diaminophenazine (DAP), a derivative of Phenazine, is a large group of nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound with diverse chemical structure and various biological activities, such as antibacterial, antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities. Phenazine is a fluorescent molecule with wide range of biological properties. Therefore, a novel chemical methodology is required for effective synthesis of this product. Numerous oxidants can easily oxidize ortho-phenylenediamine (OPD) to create luminous DAP. This article discusses a simple, sustainable, and safe way to synthesize DAP using water as a green solvent and Jeanbandyite as a catalyst. Mass spectrometry, (1)H-NMR and (13)C-NMR were used to characterize the molecule, and the catalytic efficacy of Jeanbandyite was assessed. The cellular uptake and cytotoxicity of DAP were investigated to determine whether DAP can be used as a bioprobe in bioapplications. Finally, DAP binding to DNA was methodically performed and confirmed using molecular docking.
abstract_zh: 近年来，开发用于有机化合物合成的新型化学路径引起了特别关注。2,3-二氨基吩嗪（DAP），作为吩嗪的一种衍生物，是一大类含氮杂环化合物，具有多样的化学结构和多种生物活性，如抗菌、抗微生物、抗炎和抗癌活性。吩嗪是一种具有广泛生物特性的荧光分子。因此，需要一种新颖的化学方法来有效合成该产物。多种氧化剂能轻易将邻苯二胺（OPD）氧化生成发光的DAP。本文讨论了一种简单、可持续且安全的DAP合成方法，使用水作为绿色溶剂，并以Jeanbandyite作为催化剂。通过质谱、¹H-NMR和¹³C-NMR对分子进行了表征，并评估了Jeanbandyite的催化效能。研究了DAP的细胞摄取和细胞毒性，以确定DAP是否可作为生物探针用于生物应用。最后，通过分子对接系统地进行了DAP与DNA的结合研究并予以确认。
